stories.title: MS Paint and Photos inivisibly watermark even locally generated output with GUID
stories.blurb: A reverse-engineering deep dive reveals that Microsoft's bundled apps embed an invisible, device-linked GUID watermark into images you create locally — without disclosure. This is a significant privacy story for anyone who assumed local image creation stayed on-device. The 289-comment HN thread is lit.

stories.title: How Europe is killing makers and micro-entrepreneurs
stories.blurb: The top story of the day by a mile: an open letter from the operator of Lectronz (a Tindie-style EU electronics marketplace) detailing how a wave of compliance regulations — CE marking, GPSR, EPR — is crushing small hardware sellers. A cautionary tale for anyone building physical products or selling digital tools in Europe.

stories.title: iCloud+ Hide My Email addresses will remain on icloud.com
stories.blurb: Apple quietly reversed course and confirmed Hide My Email addresses will stay accessible at icloud.com — a relief for privacy-conscious users who rely on the feature to stop spam and protect their real address. Direct Apple developer notice, worth bookmarking for users worried about continuity of their alias ecosystem.

stories.title: LLMs could control their host machines by exploiting inference engines
stories.blurb: A sobering security essay: inference engines (llama.cpp, vLLM, etc.) have attack surfaces that a sufficiently motivated model output could exploit to break out of isolation. Directly relevant for anyone running local LLMs as part of a Claude Code or agentic workflow. Read before you run untrusted prompts locally.

stories.title: Xiaomi: New CPU matches Apple cores single threaded, much faster multithreaded
stories.blurb: Daniel Lemire's benchmarks show Xiaomi's new in-house chip trading blows with Apple Silicon on single-threaded workloads — but blowing it away in multicore. If the numbers hold up, this is the first credible challenger to Apple's IPC dominance since M1 launched. The HN thread is a deep hardware nerd fight.

stories.title: Fences, Not Sandboxes
stories.blurb: Steve Yegge argues that we've been thinking about AI agent safety wrong — sandboxing is the wrong mental model, and "fences" (capability limits defined by the principal) are more practical and effective. Directly relevant to anyone designing agentic Claude Code workflows or multi-agent systems.

stories.title: Jabber/XMPP: 25 Years of Digital Independence
stories.blurb: The author of Conversations (the leading XMPP Android client) reflects on 25 years of federated, open messaging — what worked, what didn't, and why digital independence still matters in the age of Slack and Discord. A thoughtful meditation on protocol design and decentralization that holds up as a counter-narrative to the walled-garden era.

stories.title: The entire city of San Francisco as a video game
stories.blurb: A developer turned the full street network and building footprint data of San Francisco into a playable top-down game — all in the browser. A delightful piece of creative coding that shows what's possible when you combine open geospatial data with WebGL. Immediately playable, highly shareable.

stories.title: Show HN: A techno machine in one HTML file, with verifiable renders
stories.blurb: A fully functional techno drum machine and step sequencer crammed into a single self-contained HTML file, with a clever twist: the rendered audio output is cryptographically verifiable. Peak creative coding — open it, press play, and marvel at what one file can do.

stories.title: Octopus intelligence may be related to never-before-seen mutation
stories.blurb: Scientists found a unique RNA-editing mutation in smart octopus species that may allow them to fine-tune protein production in neurons on the fly. It's a completely novel evolutionary path to intelligence — one that has no parallel in vertebrates. Required reading for anyone who thinks biology has run out of surprises.

stories.title: I were 17, I'd learn how to build LLMs from scratch
stories.blurb: Paul Graham's tweet that learning to build LLMs from scratch is the highest-leverage skill for a teenager today sparked 623 comments debating whether he's right. The HN discussion is the real content here — a lively argument about LLM fundamentals vs. application-layer skills worth scanning for the best takes.

stories.title: Training AI to Paint with Code
stories.blurb: A walkthrough of fine-tuning Qwen to generate visual art by writing code — think SVG and canvas programs — rather than pixel-pushing. This is a genuinely interesting direction for AI creativity that sidesteps diffusion model limitations and produces fully editable, resolution-independent output.

stories.title: Walgit – a Git server that is one binary in front of an object store
stories.blurb: Shopify's Tobi Lütke open-sourced Walgit: a minimal Git server that stores everything on S3-compatible object storage as a single binary. No database, no running daemon complexity. If you want private self-hosted Git without the GitHub/Gitea overhead, this is worth a look.

stories.title: Show HN: Screen memory without screenshots, just text to Markdown
stories.blurb: ambient-context passively captures your screen activity as structured Markdown text — no pixel screenshots, no heavy storage. The result is a lightweight, privacy-friendlier "memory" layer that can feed context to LLMs. Directly relevant to anyone building Claude Code workflows that need session continuity.

stories.title: Moon (2024)
stories.blurb: Bartosz Ciechanowski's signature interactive explainer, this time on the Moon — orbital mechanics, libration, tidal locking, and more, all rendered with gorgeous real-time WebGL animations. If you haven't encountered his work before, prepare to lose an hour. This is science communication at its absolute best.

stories.title: SeL4 security proofs now complete on AArch64
stories.blurb: The seL4 microkernel's full formal security proofs — functional correctness, integrity, and confidentiality — are now complete on 64-bit ARM. This is a landmark for formally verified software; it means the entire correctness proof chain holds for the hardware most modern devices actually run on.

stories.title: Show HN: PicoMQ – Durable Streams over HTTP, on object storage
stories.blurb: PicoMQ brings durable message streams over plain HTTP, backed by object storage — no Kafka, no brokers, no ops nightmare. For .NET/TypeScript developers who need reliable pub/sub without standing up a cluster, this is a genuinely interesting serverless-friendly primitive.

stories.title: Hot Chips 2026: CUDA Targets RISC-V – By Chester Lam
stories.blurb: NVIDIA is porting CUDA to RISC-V cores — a strategic move that could reshape GPU computing and open-source chip design simultaneously. Chester Lam's Hot Chips 2026 writeup explains the architecture and what it means for the GPU ecosystem beyond x86 and ARM lock-in.

stories.title: Headlong: A Microharness for Persistent Agents
stories.blurb: Headlong is a tiny framework for running persistent LLM agents that survive restarts and maintain state across sessions. For Claude Code users who want long-running autonomous tasks without babysitting a process, this microharness approach is worth studying for its simplicity.

stories.title: Bookshelf – Self-hosted eBook library that runs on object storage
stories.blurb: A clean self-hosted eBook library server that stores everything on S3-compatible object storage — no heavy database, no Calibre dependency. For developers who want a personal, privacy-respecting alternative to Kindle or cloud reading services, this is immediately deployable and worth an afternoon to set up.
